1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.Nc3 a6 4.g3 b5 5.d4.strategy: Strikes in the centre at once, before Black's queenside advance gets going. After the exchange White's knight settles on d4 with the bishop on g2 to come, supporting e4, and White has an Open Sicilian in which Black's queenside pawns have already advanced.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.Nc3 a6 4.g3 b5 5.d4 c.strategy: Takes the central pawn, opening the c-file for Black's rook and removing White's chance to build a broad centre. Ignoring the challenge would let White decide how to resolve the tension, so Black captures at once.
